scientific_question: Do the three original CC0 white-stork cohorts contain sufficient non-overlapping or overlapping real time coverage for a future independently measured conspecific-opportunity test? This is tag deployment metadata, not bird co-presence.
source_licence: Original Movebank Data Repository archived DataCite records report CC0; these are only three already verified reference CSV bitstreams.

timestamp_contract.allowed: ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:SS[.ffffff]], T separator, optional Z/UTC offset; do not infer format from downstream outcomes
timestamp_contract.failed_or_blank: missing/unparseable; do not substitute last GPS observation, death date or today
timestamp_contract.treatment_of_open_end: unknown right-censoring; never pretend an end date without source or count unknown as co-present
timestamp_contract.not_animal_behavior: A tag deployment interval does not establish a bird remained at the locality, was still alive, met a conspecific, or received information.

readiness_tests: n original table rows and unique tag-id per cohort
number of complete on/off pairs and of missing/unparseable timestamps per cohort
min/max year of verified deployment-on and -off
aggregate simultaneous complete-deployment intervals within each cohort, and across cohorts, only where both start/end dates exist
any cohort with <5 complete bounded intervals is NOT_ESTIMABLE for duration overlap; no retained impression from overlapping starts alone
count of cross-cohort same tag IDs privately without exporting IDs, as a duplicate-source warning only not same-bird identity
no GPS events or environmental q are opened
analysis_rule: If no adequate complete off intervals, STOP with TIME_WINDOW_ENDS_UNOBSERVED and report source support only. Do not post-hoc set arbitrary end dates. Even positive tag deployments are not proof of biological co-travel or conspecific cue exposure.
prior_art: Brønnvik et al. 2024 Current Biology DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2024.03.052 already documents age-declining conspecific density preference; Bontekoe et al. 2023 documents treatment effects; neither is a new PAYOFF result.
